clue.text: One's taken to court to crush illegal activity

parts.note: to crush something is to squash it flat
a racket is a dishonest money-making scheme

explanation.surface: A defendant is hauled before the judges to stamp out some criminal enterprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a law court, but it is the squash court the racket is carried onto.
explanation.definitionFit: A player carries this bat-like implement onto the court for the indoor ball game.

clue.text: See 19
Blurt out rank

definitions.meaning: to blurt out words is to say or voice them suddenly
rank as an adjective means complete or absolute, as in a rank amateur

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to speak or voice; the adjective means total or out-and-out, the same sense as rank.

clue.text: Matter caught between modes of transport

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a vessel for travelling under water

indicators.note: between tells us the caught letter sits among the letters of the two vehicles

parts.note: a jet is an aircraft
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Something is trapped in the gap between two kinds of vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' is satisfied by the caught letter sitting just before the final letter of the second vehicle, not strictly between the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A subject is the topic or matter under discussion, a direct synonym.

clue.text: One of two circles, one left to turn around

indicators.note: to turn means the pair of words before it is read backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral one is I
port is the left side of a ship
C stands for circa, Latin for around, as used with dates

explanation.surface: Someone describes a geometry figure: two circles, one of which spins round to the left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' turns I + PORT into TROPI; 'around' then gives C, from circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Cancer and Capricorn are the two parallel circles of latitude either side of the equator, each one bearing this name.

clue.text: Red setter, did you say?

indicators.note: did you say asks us to hear the setter's name spoken rather than read

parts.note: Rufus is the pen name of a long-serving Guardian crossword compiler

explanation.surface: It reads as a query about a red setter, the Irish dog breed with a glossy chestnut coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red setter' looks like the dog; 'setter' is the crossword compiler Rufus, whose name is pronounced like the colour word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an uncommon term for a reddish-brown colour, used of animal fur and plumage.

clue.text: It's not worth doing, to be blunt

definitions.meaning: a futile task achieves nothing and is not worth doing
a blunt blade or pencil has lost its sharp tip

explanation.definitionFit: Futile and also, read literally, lacking a sharp tip, which is what a blunt edge is.

clue.text: Inclination to enter competition to make a great profit

indicators.note: to enter tells us the inclination goes inside the competition

parts.note: a cup is a knockout competition, such as the FA Cup
a lean is an inclination or tilt

explanation.surface: Someone tempted to enter a contest hopes to win big.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to win or earn a large sum, a big financial killing.

clue.text: Alchemists in cooking about right — to earn these?

definitions.text: Alchemists in cooking about right — to earn these?

indicators.note: about means the anagram goes round the letter for right
cooking signals the letters of the words before it are being mixed up

explanation.surface: Chefs who work kitchen alchemy and get things just right might win restaurant awards.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: cooking well is how a restaurant earns these guide ratings.
explanation.definitionFit: These stars are the prestigious ratings a famous guide awards to restaurants for outstanding cooking.

clue.text: Totally reliable friend endlessly quaffing drink

indicators.note: quaffing means swallowing, so the shortened friend takes the drink inside
endlessly means the last letter of the friend is cut off

parts.note: a crony is a close friend or pal
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A dependable pal is knocking back drinks without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont in northern Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated adjective, from the hard metal, means solid and unbreakable, as in a watertight guarantee.

clue.text: Aubrey's work as it happens in underpants

indicators.note: in tells us the broadcast word goes inside the underwear

parts.note: briefs are close-fitting underpants
a live broadcast goes out as it happens

explanation.surface: It sounds like the setter is asking what a man called Aubrey wears in his underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: John Aubrey was a 17th-century English writer whose short biographies of his contemporaries are known under this title.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of John Aubrey's famous collection of short biographical sketches.

clue.text: Stab with tip of dagger in weapon

indicators.note: in shows the dagger's tip is placed inside the weapon

parts.note: piece is slang for a gun

indicators.note: tip of takes one end letter of the word dagger, here its final one

explanation.surface: An attack with the point of a knife plunged into a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The tip used is dagger's last letter, R, not its first.
explanation.definitionFit: To stab is to puncture or penetrate with a sharp point.

clue.text: A parting pursuit involving death that's memorable

indicators.note: parting means the letter A splits the pursuit word open

parts.note: hunting is the pursuit of game

explanation.surface: A farewell chase that results in a killing and lingers in the mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving death' nods to ghosts, which return from the dead to frequent a place, and also to hunting itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A tune or image of this kind lingers unforgettably in the mind, like a ghost revisiting.

clue.text: Wearing cooler hat, not so sophisticated

parts.note: if you are in a garment you are wearing it
a fan keeps you cool
tile is old slang for a hat

explanation.surface: Someone in a silly hat with a fan seems rather less suave.
explanation.definitionFit: Childish behaviour lacks maturity and refinement, so it is unsophisticated.

clue.text: Not quite clever enough — or too much?

definitions.meaning: describes someone slightly dim or slow-witted
an idiom for something unreasonable or excessive, as in rather much to ask

explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase means somewhat stupid, and also, of behaviour, unreasonable or beyond acceptable limits.

clue.text: Pot plant planted initially on border

indicators.note: on in an across clue places the initial letter after the border

parts.note: a hem is the edge or border of a garment

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word planted

explanation.surface: A potted plant is set in at the edge of a flowerbed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannabis, slang name pot, is the drug obtained from this plant.

clue.text: Just OK

definitions.meaning: just here means even-handed and equitable

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both equitable and merely adequate, matching each clue word.

clue.text: Party girl, a bird?

definitions.meaning: a fun-loving young woman of the 1920s jazz age
something that beats its wings, or a young bird just learning to fly

explanation.definitionFit: The 1920s term named fashionable, carefree young women; literally it describes anything whose wings beat.

clue.text: Cross waves in secret to defect, ultimately

indicators.note: waves means the letters of in and secret are moved about
ultimately takes the last letter of the word defect

explanation.surface: A spy crosses the ocean in secret to defect in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves' scrambles only 'secret'; 'in' stands as written at the front, and 'Cross' is a verb, not anger.
explanation.definitionFit: Two lines that intersect cross each other at a point.

clue.text: Avenger waiting to serve God

parts.note: a president elect has been chosen but is waiting to take office
Ra is the Egyptian sun god

explanation.surface: Someone waiting on God hopes for vengeance.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this daughter of Agamemnon helps avenge her father's murder.

clue.text: In America, where one goes to monitor facts after a review

indicators.note: after a review means the letters are rearranged once looked over again

explanation.surface: An American fact-checker reviews the facts before publishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where one goes' is a coy way to say the toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A public lavatory is called this in the United States, a euphemism for where you go.

clue.text: Gas faults in need of repair

indicators.note: in need of repair suggests the word faults is broken and must be rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A gas appliance's faults mean it needs fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the medical term for intestinal wind, a gas expelled from the body.

clue.text: Sailor out of tune, that's plain

parts.note: an old salt is a veteran sailor
a flat note is below pitch, out of tune

explanation.surface: A sailor sings off-key, and that is plain to hear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' is a noun, an area of flat land, not 'obvious'.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a level expanse of land covered with salt left by an evaporated lake, a kind of plain.

clue.text: Raise the dead with word of hesitation in old man

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: in places the hesitation word within the old man

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
um is said when hesitating

explanation.surface: An old man hesitantly tries to bring the dead back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old man' does double work as two pieces, a prefix meaning former and a male pronoun, with the hesitation word inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To dig up a buried body is literally to bring a corpse back above ground.

clue.text: Raise yokel to strangle duck

indicators.note: to strangle means the yokel wraps around the duck

parts.note: a hick is an unsophisticated country person
a duck in cricket is a score of zero, which looks like O

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin lifts up a duck to wring its neck.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal verb means to lift or yank something up abruptly.

clue.text: Disease caught by pair, lots scattered in terror

indicators.note: caught by means the disease is held inside the jumbled letters
scattered tells us the letters of pair and lots are strewn in a new order

parts.note: TB is tuberculosis

explanation.surface: A disease spreads, many people are infected in a panic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terror' means a badly behaved child, not fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A little terror is an unruly child, and an indulged, badly behaved child is exactly that.

clue.text: See 9
Dissolute king half consumed by evidence of herpes?

indicators.note: consumed by means the half king is swallowed by the skin sign

parts.note: a rash is a visible sign of the infection

indicators.note: half takes the first two letters of the word king

explanation.surface: A debauched monarch half eaten away by signs of a sexually transmitted infection.
explanation.definitionFit: A rakish man is a rake, a womanising and dissolute pleasure-seeker.

clue.text: See 1
